title: AVERAGE: mean of a score list

screens.prompt: In B7, work out the class average of the five scores.

hints.syntax: =AVERAGE(B2:B6): one function, one range, no plus signs.
hints.func-average: Use AVERAGE. Adding the scores and dividing by five by hand works here and breaks the moment a student leaves.
hints.require-ref: Point the formula at the score column instead of typing the number you worked out.
hints.value: The answer is 88.5. Check that the range covers all five scores and nothing else.
hints.error: #DIV/0! means AVERAGE found no numbers at all: the range is pointing at blank cells or at the header word rather than at the five scores. Text is skipped silently, not averaged.
hints.hardcoded: The formula only works for these five scores, which means a number is typed in. Average the whole range, B2:B6, so a corrected score moves the class average.

reject.why: the arithmetic is right but SUM is not AVERAGE
types the scores into AVERAGE instead of pointing at B2:B6
averages one score and pads it with 3.5, so Ana going up a point misses the average

variants.why: Ana goes from 85 to 86, so the average has to move with her
Bo goes from 90 to 91, so the average has to move with him
Cy goes from 88 to 89, so the average has to move with him

docs.explain:
AVERAGE adds the numbers in a range and divides by how many it found. The five scores here are 85, 90, 88, 92 and 87.5, which come to 442.5, so the answer is 88.5. The divisor is the count of cells holding a number, not the count of rows. A blank cell is skipped; a zero is not.

This exercise wants the class average in B7, taken from B2:B6. Every score is present, so nothing is skipped and the answer lands on 88.5. The count is where a typed sum goes wrong: a sixth student with no score yet leaves AVERAGE dividing by five, while SUM(B2:B6)/6 drags the mean down.

Point the formula at the range instead of typing the five numbers. A corrected score then moves the average on its own, and a student who leaves the class stops counting without anyone editing the formula.

errors.text: The range holds no numbers at all, so there is nothing to divide by: usually the formula points at the names column or at blank cells.
A word or symbol was handed to AVERAGE as an argument, as in =AVERAGE("n/a"); text sitting inside a range is skipped instead.
A total divided by a typed 6 keeps dividing by 6 after a student leaves, and the mean slides away from the scores.

docs.atWork: Class averages and average order value: one function covers both, and it keeps its count straight when a row is empty.
docs.outcome: Turn five scores into one class average that updates itself.

seo.title: AVERAGE in Excel: the mean of a column
seo.description: AVERAGE divides the total by the count of numbers, so a blank cell never drags the mean down. Five scores average 88.5, and the page shows why.
